title: To This Day ... for the bullied and beautiful
speaker: Shane Koyczan

sentences.en: Translator: Joseph Geni Reviewer: Morton Bast There's so many of you.
sentences.zh: 译者：Joseph Geni 审稿人：Morton Bast 你们这么多人。

sentences.en: (Laughter) When I was a kid, I hid my heart under the bed, because my mother said, "If you're not careful, someday someone's going to break it."
sentences.zh: （笑声）当我还是个孩子的时候，我把我的心藏在床底下，因为我妈妈说：“如果你不小心，有一天就会有人打破它。”

sentences.en: Take it from me: Under the bed is not a good hiding spot.
sentences.zh: 请相信我：床底下不是一个好的藏身之处。

sentences.en: I know because I've been shot down so many times, I get altitude sickness just from standing up for myself.
sentences.zh: 我知道，因为我被击落了很多次，所以我只要站起来就会出现高原反应。

sentences.en: But that's what we were told. "Stand up for yourself."
sentences.zh: 但这就是我们被告知的。 “为自己挺身而出。”

sentences.en: And that's hard to do if you don't know who you are.
sentences.zh: 如果你不知道自己是谁，那就很难做到。

sentences.en: We were expected to define ourselves at such an early age, and if we didn't do it, others did it for us.
sentences.zh: 人们期望我们在很小的时候就定义自己，如果我们不这样做，别人就会替我们做。

sentences.en: Geek. Fatty. Slut. Fag. And at the same time we were being told what we were, we were being asked, "What do you want to be when you grow up?"
sentences.zh: 极客。胖子。荡妇。基佬。与此同时，我们被告知我们是谁，我们被问到：“你长大后想做什么？”

sentences.en: I always thought that was an unfair question.
sentences.zh: 我一直认为这是一个不公平的问题。

sentences.en: It presupposes that we can't be what we already are.
sentences.zh: 它的前提是我们不能成为现在的样子。

sentences.en: We were kids. When I was a kid, I wanted to be a man.
sentences.zh: 我们还是孩子。当我还是个孩子的时候，我想成为一个男人。

sentences.en: I wanted a registered retirement savings plan that would keep me in candy long enough to make old age sweet.
sentences.zh: 我想要一个注册的退休储蓄计划，让我能在足够长的时间内享受甜蜜的生活，让晚年变得甜蜜。

sentences.en: (Laughter) When I was a kid, I wanted to shave.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 当我还是个孩子的时候，我想刮胡子。

sentences.en: Now, not so much. (Laughter) When I was eight, I wanted to be a marine biologist.
sentences.zh: 现在，没那么多了。 （笑声）当我八岁时，我想成为一名海洋生物学家。

sentences.en: When I was nine, I saw the movie "Jaws," and thought to myself, "No, thank you."
sentences.zh: 当我九岁的时候，我看了电影《大白鲨》，心里想：“不，谢谢。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) And when I was 10, I was told that my parents left because they didn't want me.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 当我 10 岁的时候，我被告知我的父母离开了，因为他们不想要我了。

sentences.en: When I was 11, I wanted to be left alone.
sentences.zh: 当我11岁的时候，我想一个人呆着。

sentences.en: When I was 12, I wanted to die. When I was 13, I wanted to kill a kid.
sentences.zh: 当我12岁的时候，我想死。当我13岁的时候，我想杀死一个孩子。

sentences.en: When I was 14, I was asked to seriously consider a career path.
sentences.zh: 当我 14 岁时，我被要求认真考虑职业道路。

sentences.en: I said, "I'd like to be a writer." And they said, "Choose something realistic."
sentences.zh: 我说：“我想成为一名作家。”他们说：“选择一些现实的东西。”

sentences.en: So I said, "Professional wrestler." And they said, "Don't be stupid."
sentences.zh: 所以我说：“职业摔跤手。”他们说：“别犯傻了。”

sentences.en: See, they asked me what I wanted to be, then told me what not to be.
sentences.zh: 看，他们问我想做什么，然后告诉我不该做什么。

sentences.en: And I wasn't the only one. We were being told that we somehow must become what we are not, sacrificing what we are to inherit the masquerade of what we will be.
sentences.zh: 而且我不是唯一一个。我们被告知，我们必须以某种方式成为我们所不是的，牺牲我们现在的样子，才能继承我们将要成为的样子。

sentences.en: I was being told to accept the identity that others will give me.
sentences.zh: 我被告知要接受别人给我的身份。

sentences.en: And I wondered, what made my dreams so easy to dismiss?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，是什么让我的梦想如此容易被放弃？

sentences.en: Granted, my dreams are shy, because they're Canadian.
sentences.zh: 诚然，我的梦想是害羞的，因为它们是加拿大的。

sentences.en: (Laughter) My dreams are self-conscious and overly apologetic.
sentences.zh: （笑声）我的梦想是自我意识和过度歉意的。

sentences.en: They're standing alone at the high school dance, and they've never been kissed.
sentences.zh: 他们独自站在高中舞会上，而且从未被亲吻过。

sentences.en: See, my dreams got called names too. Silly. Foolish.
sentences.zh: 看，我的梦想也被命名了。愚蠢的。愚蠢的。

sentences.en: Impossible. But I kept dreaming. I was going to be a wrestler. I had it all figured out.
sentences.zh: 不可能的。但我一直在做梦。我本来想成为一名摔跤手。我已经全部弄清楚了。

sentences.en: I was going to be The Garbage Man. (Laughter) My finishing move was going to be The Trash Compactor.
sentences.zh: 我本来想成为垃圾人。 （笑声）我的最后一步是垃圾压实机。

sentences.en: My saying was going to be, "I'm taking out the trash!"
sentences.zh: 我的原话是：“我要去倒垃圾！”

sentences.en: (Laughter) (Applause) And then this guy, Duke "The Dumpster" Droese, stole my entire shtick.
sentences.zh: （笑声）（掌声）然后这个家伙，“垃圾箱”杜克·德罗斯，偷走了我的全部技巧。

sentences.en: (Laughter) I was crushed, as if by a trash compactor.
sentences.zh: （笑声）我被压碎了，就像被垃圾压实机压碎了一样。

sentences.en: (Laughter) I thought to myself, "What now? Where do I turn?"
sentences.zh: （笑声）我心想：“现在怎么办？我该去哪里？”

sentences.en: Poetry. (Laughter) Like a boomerang, the thing I loved came back to me.
sentences.zh: 诗。 （笑声） 就像回旋镖一样，我所爱的东西又回到了我身边。

sentences.en: One of the first lines of poetry I can remember writing was in response to a world that demanded I hate myself.
sentences.zh: 我记得写的第一行诗是对一个要求我憎恨自己的世界的回应。

sentences.en: From age 15 to 18, I hated myself for becoming the thing that I loathed: a bully.
sentences.zh: 从 15 岁到 18 岁，我讨厌自己变成了我讨厌的人：一个恶霸。

sentences.en: When I was 19, I wrote, "I will love myself despite the ease with which I lean toward the opposite."
sentences.zh: 当我 19 岁时，我写道：“尽管我很容易倾向于相反的观点，但我会爱自己。”

sentences.en: Standing up for yourself doesn't have to mean embracing violence.
sentences.zh: 为自己挺身而出并不一定意味着拥抱暴力。

sentences.en: When I was a kid, I traded in homework assignments for friendship, then gave each friend a late slip for never showing up on time, and in most cases, not at all.
sentences.zh: 当我还是个孩子的时候，我用家庭作业换取友谊，然后给每个朋友一张迟到单，因为他们没有准时出现，而且在大多数情况下，根本没有。

sentences.en: I gave myself a hall pass to get through each broken promise.
sentences.zh: 我给自己开了一张大厅通行证，以兑现每一个违背的承诺。

sentences.en: And I remember this plan, born out of frustration from a kid who kept calling me "Yogi," then pointed at my tummy and said, "Too many picnic baskets."
sentences.zh: 我记得这个计划是出于一个孩子的挫败感而诞生的，他一直叫我“瑜伽士”，然后指着我的肚子说：“野餐篮子太多了。”

sentences.en: Turns out it's not that hard to trick someone, and one day before class, I said, "Yeah, you can copy my homework," and I gave him all the wrong answers that I'd written down the night before.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，欺骗某人并不难，有一天上课前，我说：“是的，你可以抄我的作业。”然后我把前一天晚上写下的所有错误答案都给了他。

sentences.en: He got his paper back expecting a near-perfect score, and couldn't believe it when he looked across the room at me and held up a zero.
sentences.zh: 他拿回卷子，期待着一个近乎满分的分数，当他看着房间另一边的我并举起一个零时，他简直不敢相信。

sentences.en: I knew I didn't have to hold up my paper of 28 out of 30, but my satisfaction was complete when he looked at me, puzzled, and I thought to myself, "Smarter than the average bear, motherfucker."
sentences.zh: 我知道我不必举起我的试卷（满分 30 分中的 28 分），但当他困惑地看着我时，我感到非常满意，我心想：“比一般的熊聪明，混蛋。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) (Applause) This is who I am. This is how I stand up for myself.
sentences.zh: （笑声）（掌声）这就是我。这就是我为自己辩护的方式。

sentences.en: When I was a kid, I used to think that pork chops and karate chops were the same thing.
sentences.zh: 小时候，我一直以为猪排和空手道排是同一种东西。

sentences.en: I thought they were both pork chops. My grandmother thought it was cute, and because they were my favorite, she let me keep doing it.
sentences.zh: 我以为它们都是猪排。我祖母觉得这很可爱，因为它们是我的最爱，所以她让我继续做。

sentences.en: Not really a big deal. One day, before I realized fat kids are not designed to climb trees, I fell out of a tree and bruised the right side of my body.
sentences.zh: 没什么大不了的。有一天，在我意识到胖孩子不适合爬树之前，我从树上摔下来，身体右侧擦伤。

sentences.en: I didn't want to tell my grandmother because I was scared I'd get in trouble for playing somewhere I shouldn't have been.
sentences.zh: 我不想告诉我的祖母，因为我害怕我会因为去不该去的地方玩而惹上麻烦。

sentences.en: The gym teacher noticed the bruise, and I got sent to the principal's office.
sentences.zh: 体育老师注意到了我的瘀伤，把我送到了校长办公室。

sentences.en: From there, I was sent to another small room with a really nice lady who asked me all kinds of questions about my life at home.
sentences.zh: 从那里，我被送到另一个小房间，里面有一位非常好的女士，她问了我关于家里生活的各种问题。

sentences.en: I saw no reason to lie. As far as I was concerned, life was pretty good.
sentences.zh: 我认为没有理由撒谎。就我而言，生活已经很美好了。

sentences.en: I told her, whenever I'm sad, my grandmother gives me karate chops.
sentences.zh: 我告诉她，每当我难过的时候，奶奶就会给我空手道排骨。

sentences.en: (Laughter) This led to a full-scale investigation, and I was removed from the house for three days,
sentences.zh: （笑声）这导致了全面调查，我被赶出家门三天，

sentences.en: until they finally decided to ask how I got the bruises.
sentences.zh: 直到他们最终决定问我这些瘀伤是怎么来的。

sentences.en: News of this silly little story quickly spread through the school, and I earned my first nickname: Porkchop.
sentences.zh: 这个愚蠢的小故事的消息很快传遍了学校，我赢得了我的第一个绰号：猪排。

sentences.en: To this day, I hate pork chops. I'm not the only kid who grew up this way, surrounded by people who used to say that rhyme
sentences.zh: 直到今天，我还是讨厌猪排。我不是唯一一个这样长大的孩子，周围都是曾经说过这句押韵的人

sentences.en: about sticks and stones, as if broken bones hurt more than the names we got called, and we got called them all.
sentences.zh: 关于棍棒和石头，好像骨折比我们被叫的名字更痛苦，我们都被叫了。

sentences.en: So we grew up believing no one would ever fall in love with us, that we'd be lonely forever, that we'd never meet someone to make us feel like the sun was something they built for us in their toolshed.
sentences.zh: 所以我们从小就相信没有人会爱上我们，我们会永远孤独，我们永远不会遇到让我们觉得太阳是他们在工具棚里为我们建造的东西的人。

sentences.en: So broken heartstrings bled the blues, and we tried to empty ourselves so we'd feel nothing.
sentences.zh: 破碎的心弦流淌着忧郁的血，我们试图清空自己，这样我们就什么也感觉不到了。

sentences.en: Don't tell me that hurts less than a broken bone, that an ingrown life is something surgeons can cut away, that there's no way for it to metastasize; it does.
sentences.zh: 别告诉我这比断骨更疼，外科医生可以切除内生的生命，它无法转移；确实如此。

sentences.en: She was eight years old, our first day of grade three when she got called ugly.
sentences.zh: 她八岁那年，我们上三年级的第一天，她就被说丑了。

sentences.en: We both got moved to the back of class so we would stop getting bombarded by spitballs.
sentences.zh: 我们俩都被转移到教室后面，这样我们就不会被纸团轰炸了。

sentences.en: But the school halls were a battleground.
sentences.zh: 但学校礼堂却是一个战场。

sentences.en: We found ourselves outnumbered day after wretched day.
sentences.zh: 我们发现自己寡不敌众，日子一天天过去。

sentences.en: We used to stay inside for recess, because outside was worse.
sentences.zh: 我们过去常常呆在室内休息，因为外面的情况更糟。

sentences.en: Outside, we'd have to rehearse running away, or learn to stay still like statues, giving no clues that we were there.
sentences.zh: 在外面，我们必须排练逃跑，或者学会像雕像一样保持静止，不让任何人知道我们在那里。

sentences.en: In grade five, they taped a sign to the front of her desk that read, "Beware of dog."
sentences.zh: 五年级时，他们在她的课桌前面贴了一个牌子，上面写着“小心狗”。

sentences.en: To this day, despite a loving husband, she doesn't think she's beautiful, because of a birthmark that takes up a little less than half her face.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，尽管有一个慈爱的丈夫，她仍然认为自己并不美丽，因为胎记占据了她不到一半的脸。

sentences.en: Kids used to say, "She looks like a wrong answer that someone tried to erase, but couldn't quite get the job done."
sentences.zh: 孩子们常常说，“她看起来像是一个错误的答案，有人试图抹去，但无法完全完成工作。”

sentences.en: And they'll never understand that she's raising two kids whose definition of beauty begins with the word "Mom," because they see her heart before they see her skin, because she's only ever always been amazing.
sentences.zh: 他们永远不会明白，她养育的两个孩子对美丽的定义都是从“妈妈”这个词开始的，因为他们在看到她的皮肤之前先看到了她的心，因为她总是令人惊叹。

sentences.en: He was a broken branch grafted onto a different family tree, adopted, not because his parents opted for a different destiny.
sentences.zh: 他是一根折断的树枝，被嫁接到不同的家谱上，被收养，并不是因为他的父母选择了不同的命运。

sentences.en: He was three when he became a mixed drink of one part left alone and two parts tragedy, started therapy in eighth grade, had a personality made up of tests and pills, lived like the uphills were mountains and the downhills were cliffs,
sentences.zh: 当他三岁时，他变成了一半孤独，两部分悲剧的混合饮料，八年级开始接受治疗，性格由测试和药物组成，生活就像上坡是山脉，下坡是悬崖，

sentences.en: four-fifths suicidal, a tidal wave of antidepressants, and an adolescent being called "Popper," one part because of the pills, 99 parts because of the cruelty.
sentences.zh: 五分之四的人有自杀倾向，抗抑郁药如潮水般涌来，一名青少年被称为“波普尔”，一部分是因为药物，九十九部分是因为残酷。

sentences.en: He tried to kill himself in grade 10 when a kid who could still go home to Mom and Dad had the audacity to tell him, "Get over it."
sentences.zh: 十年级时，他试图自杀，当时一个仍然可以回家见爸爸妈妈的孩子竟然厚颜无耻地告诉他：“别介意了。”

sentences.en: As if depression is something that could be remedied by any of the contents found in a first-aid kit.
sentences.zh: 就好像抑郁症是可以通过急救箱中的任何内容来治愈的一样。

sentences.en: To this day, he is a stick of TNT lit from both ends, could describe to you in detail the way the sky bends in the moment before it's about to fall, and despite an army of friends who all call him an inspiration, he remains a conversation piece between people who can't understand
sentences.zh: 直到今天，他还是一根两端点燃的 TNT 棍子，可以向你详细描述天空在即将坠落前的那一刻是如何弯曲的，尽管有一大群朋友都称他为灵感来源，但他仍然是无法理解的人之间的话题。

sentences.en: sometimes being drug-free has less to do with addiction and more to do with sanity.
sentences.zh: 有时戒毒与成瘾关系不大，而与理智关系更大。

sentences.en: We weren't the only kids who grew up this way.
sentences.zh: 我们并不是唯一这样长大的孩子。

sentences.en: To this day, kids are still being called names.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，孩子们仍然被辱骂。

sentences.en: The classics were "Hey, stupid," "Hey, spaz."
sentences.zh: 经典的歌曲是“嘿，笨蛋”，“嘿，傻瓜”。

sentences.en: Seems like every school has an arsenal of names getting updated every year.
sentences.zh: 似乎每所学校都有一个每年都会更新的名称库。

sentences.en: And if a kid breaks in a school and no one around chooses to hear, do they make a sound?
sentences.zh: 如果一个孩子闯入学校而周围没有人愿意听到，他们会发出声音吗？

sentences.en: Are they just background noise from a soundtrack stuck on repeat, when people say things like, "Kids can be cruel."
sentences.zh: 当人们说“孩子可能很残忍”之类的话时，它们只是重复播放的配乐中的背景噪音吗？

sentences.en: Every school was a big top circus tent, and the pecking order went from acrobats to lion tamers, from clowns to carnies, all of these miles ahead of who we were.
sentences.zh: 每所学校都是一个巨大的顶级马戏团帐篷，等级顺序从杂技演员到驯狮员，从小丑到狂欢节，所有这些都比我们领先了很多英里。

sentences.en: We were freaks -- lobster-claw boys and bearded ladies, oddities juggling depression and loneliness, playing solitaire, spin the bottle, trying to kiss the wounded parts of ourselves and heal, but at night, while the others slept,
sentences.zh: 我们是怪人——龙虾爪男孩和留着胡子的女士，在抑郁和孤独之间周旋的怪人，玩纸牌游戏，旋转瓶子，试图亲吻自己受伤的部分并治愈，但在晚上，当其他人睡觉时，

sentences.en: we kept walking the tightrope. It was practice, and yes, some of us fell.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在走钢丝。这是练习，是的，我们中的一些人跌倒了。

sentences.en: But I want to tell them that all of this is just debris left over when we finally decide to smash all the things we thought we used to be, and if you can't see anything beautiful about yourself,
sentences.zh: 但我想告诉他们，这一切都只是当我们最终决定粉碎所有我们认为曾经的东西时留下的碎片，如果你看不到自己的美丽，

sentences.en: get a better mirror, look a little closer, stare a little longer, because there's something inside you that made you keep trying despite everyone who told you to quit.
sentences.zh: 找一面更好的镜子，看得近一点，凝视久一点，因为你内心有某种东西让你继续努力，尽管每个人都告诉你放弃。

sentences.en: You built a cast around your broken heart and signed it yourself, "They were wrong."
sentences.zh: 你为你破碎的心建立了一个模型，并亲自签名：“他们错了。”

sentences.en: Because maybe you didn't belong to a group or a clique.
sentences.zh: 因为也许你不属于某个团体或派系。

sentences.en: Maybe they decided to pick you last for basketball or everything.
sentences.zh: 也许他们决定最后选你参加篮球比赛或其他比赛。

sentences.en: Maybe you used to bring bruises and broken teeth to show-and-tell, but never told, because how can you hold your ground if everyone around you wants to bury you beneath it?
sentences.zh: 也许你曾经带着瘀伤和破碎的牙齿来展示和讲述，但从未告诉过，因为如果你周围的每个人都想把你埋在它下面，你怎么能坚持自己的立场呢？

sentences.en: You have to believe that they were wrong.
sentences.zh: 你必须相信他们错了。

sentences.en: They have to be wrong. Why else would we still be here?
sentences.zh: 他们一定是错的。否则我们为什么还在这里？

sentences.en: We grew up learning to cheer on the underdog because we see ourselves in them.
sentences.zh: 我们从小就学会为失败者加油，因为我们在他们身上看到了自己。

sentences.en: We stem from a root planted in the belief that we are not what we were called.
sentences.zh: 我们的根植于这样的信念：我们并非我们所称的那样。

sentences.en: We are not abandoned cars stalled out and sitting empty on some highway, and if in some way we are, don't worry.
sentences.zh: 我们不是停在高速公路上的废弃汽车，如果在某种程度上我们是这样，请不要担心。

sentences.en: We only got out to walk and get gas. We are graduating members from the class of We Made It, not the faded echoes of voices crying out, "Names will never hurt me."
sentences.zh: 我们只是出去走路去加油。我们是“我们做到了”班级的毕业生，而不是那些呼喊着“名字永远不会伤害我”的声音的回声。

sentences.en: Of course they did. But our lives will only ever always continue to be a balancing act that has less to do with pain and more to do with beauty.
sentences.zh: 他们当然做到了。但我们的生活只会永远保持平衡，与痛苦无关，而与美丽有关。

sentences.en: (Applause)
sentences.zh: （掌声）
